# HapticService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("HapticService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

Controls vibration: the motors of a gamepad and the vibration of a phone.

`SetMotor` runs a motor at a level until it is set again, and 0 stops it. An engine that rumbles while it runs needs one call when it starts and one when it stops. `Vibrate` makes a phone vibrate for a short time and stop by itself.

A headset's controller vibrates under `Enum.UserInputType.XRLeft` or `XRRight`. It has one motor, which `SetMotor` runs whichever motor is named.

Every motor stops while the game's window is not in front, resumes when it is again, and stops when the game closes. On a dedicated server or in a headless run, every query returns false and every call is ignored.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Methods

### `IsMotorSupported(inputType: Enum.UserInputType, motor: Enum.VibrationMotor): boolean`

Returns whether a particular motor exists. Most gamepads have `Large` and `Small`, and a few have motors in their triggers. A phone has none of these; use `Vibrate` for it.

### `IsVibrationSupported(inputType: Enum.UserInputType): boolean`

Returns whether a kind of device can vibrate on this machine at present. Pass `Enum.UserInputType.Gamepad` for a connected gamepad with motors, or `Enum.UserInputType.Touch` for the device itself, such as a phone. Returns false for any other value.

### `SetMotor(inputType: Enum.UserInputType, motor: Enum.VibrationMotor, value: number)`

Runs one motor of every connected gamepad at `value`, from 0 (stopped) to 1 (full strength), until it is set again. A motor that does not exist is ignored, so there is no need to check first.

### `Vibrate(strength: number, seconds: number)`

Vibrates the device itself, such as a phone, at `strength` (0 to 1) for `seconds`, up to 5. It is ignored on a machine that cannot vibrate.
